episodes.212946: A persistent and highly moisture-laden tropical pattern set the stage for the flash flooding event from June 19-21. Thunderstorms initially developed along the Sierra Madre Oriental and crossed into South Texas on June 19, encountering an environment characterized by extremely high precipitable water values of 2.2-2.5+ inches, extreme instability with CAPE often exceeding 2,500-4,500 J/kg, and weak steering winds. As a stubborn upper-level closed low became established over South Texas, deep tropical moisture continued streaming inland on persistent southeast to east onshore flow. Multiple outflow boundaries, a mid-level vorticity maximum, and the sea breeze provided repeated lifting mechanisms for thunderstorm development. With storm motions generally under 10-15 kt and low-level inflow often stronger than the steering flow, thunderstorms repeatedly back-built, trained, and regenerated over the same locations. Rainfall rates of 2-3+ inches per hour became common, while saturated soils from prior heavy rainfall further reduced infiltration capacity. The combination of near-record atmospheric moisture, slow-moving and training thunderstorms, and several rounds of convection associated with the stationary upper low ultimately led to widespread flash flooding concerns across South Texas and the Coastal Bend through June 21.
episodes.213096: The 21st late day brought a quickly-evolving set-up featuring an increasingly moist column supported by an approaching Middle Mississippi Valley upper short wave trough, strengthening flow amid a warm frontal zone draped over the local central Indiana region providing 35-50KT of effective wind shear, and advection of higher low-level dewpoints with daytime heating which provided sufficient destabilization.  Severe rotating supercells tracked across Illinois into southern central Indiana as they aligned into a Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV).||Wind damage occurred within nine central Indiana zones and as far east as Brown County, five (mainly EF-0) tornadoes were focused in Owen County and points south and west, while the region's farthest southwestern counties experienced scattered flash flooding following downpours from multiple supercells.  A final EF-0 torando and flash flooding also occurred in Bartholomew County.  This Bartholomew County EF-0 was Indiana's 63rd tornado in 2026...a new yearly state tornado record (73 events) was set later in the evening, with 74 tallied by the end of June 21st.
episodes.213133: A convective complex moved through the region during the day on June 21st. Though it remained sub-severe for most of its life, the complex did intensify in south-central Illinois where it produced tornadoes, wind damage, and flash flooding.
episodes.213642: A few isolated Severe Thunderstorms were observed during the early to middle afternoon on June 21st. Hail was the primary hazard observed.
episodes.213670: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across central and southeast Wyoming as a strong cold front moved across the state. Several areas had multiple lines move through the same region during the event. Severe Thunderstorm Watch was in effect for most of the afternoon through the late evening hours.
episodes.214009: A frontal boundary dropping southward on the 19th of June, combined with both weak upper level support with a mid level trough of low pressure and remnant moisture from Post Tropical Cyclone Arthur moving across the area from the Gulf Coast, resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across the JAX CWA. Isolated thunderstorm damage occurred, however the primary impacts to the region was areas of flooding due to very heavy rainfall.
episodes.214016: A summer pattern of south to southwestern mean flow, combined with impacts from both the Gulf and Atlantic sea breezes and PWATs near or above 2 inches, resulted in numerous thunderstorms across northeast FL.
episodes.214054: Atlantic high pressure ridge axis remained over the eastern Gulf, central FL and into the western Atlantic maintaining a moist west-southwest low level flow for the area. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed each afternoon along the sea breezes with the strongest activity along boundary mergers. A weak cool front gradually moved southward through the area on Tuesday with a weak prefrontal trough from southwest to northeast over the region. Deeper moisture plume coincided with the frontal boundary with the strongest storms along the sea breeze and frontal interactions.
episodes.214172: Storms produced strong winds over the Southeast Texas bays.
episodes.214468: Thunderstorms tracked across eastern Colorado during the afternoon and evening hours of the 20th. A couple of the storms became severe with hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.214656: A slow moving frontal boundary affected the area during the June 18-22 period with multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms. Some severe weather was reported along with flash flooding.
episodes.214661: A typical summertime pattern produced scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms with occasional severe weather reported.
episodes.214940: A remnant Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) interacted with a sheared and unstable environment to produce numerous supercells in southeast Illinois on June 21st.  13 tornadoes were documented, the strongest being two EF-2 tornadoes near Newton.  Storms training over the same areas led to widespread heavy rainfall and several occurrences of flash flooding.
episodes.215014: Thunderstorms developed around midday over the central Nebraska Panhandle. This activity tracked to the east and southeast into the evening hours, producing numerous damaging wind and large hail reports. The greatest damage was at the eastern end of Lake McConaughy. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 81 MPH were reported. Hail up to golf ball size was reported near Imperial.
episodes.215015: A weak convective complex moved through the region during the early afternoon. Just as it was exiting, one final storm formed over St Louis County. Although this storm was small, it managed to produce a tornado.
episodes.215068: Storms that developed produced wind gusts across Campbell county.
episodes.215224: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms impacted northwest Kansas from the mid-afternoon hours through the late evening hours on the 20th, in vicinity of deepening low pressure over eastern Colorado. Thunderstorms started out as more isolated and moved eastward. With time, thunderstorms congealed into a large complex and moved more southeastward. High amounts of atmospheric instability and wind shear supported several higher-end severe weather reports, including baseball size hail in Sheridan County, and up to 100 mph winds in Thomas County.  The inflow winds with the thunderstorm complex were so high they caused dust storm conditions.  Dust storm conditions also occurred with the outflow winds from the thunderstorm complex.  These thunderstorms also produced high rainfall rates for a prolonged amount of time.  This led to flash flooding of a magnitude that had not been seen in decades.
episodes.215253: An intense complex of thunderstorms moved across portions of central and south-central Kansas during the late evening hours of June 20th into the morning hours of June 21st. Several reports of damaging winds were gathered along with a brief tornado near the Harvey-Sedgwick County line.
episodes.215270: An upper level shortwave moved over Wyoming, accompanied by a jet streak. The surface dew points remained low, resulting in large dew point depressions. The result was many severe thunderstorms that produced wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
episodes.215326: Isolated strong summer thunderstorms formed during the afternoon in central Wyoming.
episodes.215508: A few clusters of thunderstorms moved east to southeast across portions of northeast and east-central Colorado from the mid-afternoon through the early evening hours on the 21st, in vicinity of a dryline and warm front intersection. Wind gusts up to 67 mph occurred in Yuma County, and nickel sized hail occurred in Cheyenne County.
episodes.215509: A supercell tracked southeast across northeast Dundy and western Hitchcock counties during the afternoon hours on the 21st. The supercell produced hail slightly larger than three inches in diameter in Dundy County.
episodes.215511: During the early evening hours on the 21st, a few clusters of thunderstorms moved southeast across portions of northwest Kansas. Hail up to one inch in diameter occurred in Thomas County, and wind gusts up to 70 mph occurred in Wichita County, downing numerous power poles.  A short lived tornado occurred in far northwest Thomas County on the leading edge of one of the storms.
episodes.215700: A very moist airmass fueled slow moving storms in southeast Texas. Flooding was reported.
episodes.215802: Diurnal convection interacted with a very moist atmosphere across portions of Louisiana. These slow moving storms produced flooding and a report of damage.
episodes.215914: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Space and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.215930: An upper-level disturbance permitted an unsettled weather pattern to remain over South Florida and the nearby waters for a portion of late June 2026.
episodes.215931: An upper-level disturbance permitted an unsettled weather pattern to remain over South Florida and the nearby waters for a portion of late June 2026.
episodes.216034: Thunderstorms propagated along an outflow boundary southward off the southeastern Everglades and across the far upper Florida Keys, producing gale-force wind gusts.

A brief tornado developed and quickly intensified over one property. The brunt of the damage was to a double wide manufactured home that was bolted to a poured basement foundation. This home was lifted and completely taken apart with the frame bent and twisted. Unfortunately there was a fatality for this resident who was thrown in the field to the north of the property. Most of the debris from the home and two outbuildings was pushed to the northeast into an open field and could be found for six miles to the northeast. A neighboring house to the west had damage to the edge of the roof and siding from debris tossed into it, but there wasn't other damage to that property. The power pole was still upright, but the lines had been taken down. There were no remaining cedar trees on the north side of the property as viewed from satellite and street view which were part of the debris to the northeast.

The tornado started in northern Sedgwick County and crossed into southern Harvey County. Debris from the damage to the home in Sedgwick was strewn into the field and for six miles to the northeast.
